name: Chocho de Santa Catarina Ocotlán
catalog_citation: Mock, Carol. 1977. Chocho de Santa Catarina Ocotlán, Oaxaca. Archivo de Lenguas Indígenas de México 4. México: El Colegio de México.
catalog_quote: Acento. Cada palabra tiene una sílaba tónica, generalmente la penúltima, en cuyo caso no la marcamos en la ortografía. Cuando el acento cae en otra sílaba, se marca con /ˈ/ ante la sílaba acentuada. acento en la penúltima: kąθē 'palma' ... acento final: kàˈnià 'petate'

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim on the held page image of Mock 1977 p. 25; it is the entire accent statement in the book (scanned sweep of all 154 held pages). (2) The deciding source is a 1977 ALIM questionnaire sketch by a professional linguist, held in full; the classification (penultimate default, weight-blind, lexically marked exceptions incl. final stress) follows directly from it. (3) A newer and fuller description exists and is not held: Veerman-Leichsenring's 2000 reference grammar of the same village variety (xiii+140 pp), plus her IJAL 2000 pp. 321-322 stress discussion; neither is open access. (4) Open literature fetched sources now (Adamou 2025 Popolocan survey chapter, DiCanio & Bennett 2018 Mesoamerican prosody survey, DiCanio 2012 Ixcatec talk) is silent on Chocho stress position but reports penultimate stress for the sister language Metzontla Popoloca and penult-default for Ixcatec, con
audit.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: re-opened the held page image (Mock 1977, printed p. 25, heading 'Acento'). It reads verbatim 'Cada palabra tiene una sílaba tónica, generalmente la penúltima, en cuyo caso no la marcamos en la ortografía. Cuando el acento cae en otra sílaba, se marca con /ˈ/ ante la sílaba acentuada.' with the two tabulated examples 'acento en la penúltima: ką́θē 'palma'' and 'acento final: kàˈnià 'petate''. The catalog record's ellipses only bridge the table layout; quote confirmed. scanned sweep of the 154 held ALIM pages : 'Acento' as a heading

sources.citation: Adamou, Evangelia. 2025. The Popolocan languages. In Søren Wichmann (ed.), Languages and Linguistics of Mexico and Northern Central America: A Comprehensive Guide, 415-456. Berlin: De Gruyter. (author manuscript, HAL halshs-03153566)
sources.quote: No statement of stress position for Chocho. Says stress is contrastive/penultimate in Metzontla Popoloc (Veerman-Leichsenring 1991: 36-38: '(CV)CVCV pattern with stress on the penultimate vowel') and that 'Veerman-Leichsenring (2000b: 321-322) argues that Popoloc, Chocho, and Ixcatec also have stress in monosyllabic words, phonetically realized as vowel gemination, disyllabic realization of a diphthong or through the addition of an affix as a prothetic vowel.' Mazatec stress final.
sources.locator: ms. p. 8, §2.5 'Stress'; ms. p. 3 (history of research on Chocho: Belmar 1899, Mock 1977, Mock 1982, Veerman-Leichsenring 2000a)

sources.quote: Ixcatec stress penultimate (common) or final (rare) in the root; compares Mezontla/Tlacoyalco/Atzingo Popoloca; nothing on Chocho stress.
